verdict: Cheap and simple HR16 engine, but the Jatco CVT (2015 Versa) is the weak link; at 199k miles it is on borrowed time. Low purchase price does not offset CVT risk for a family car.
major_issues: Jatco CVT judder/whine/failure (CarComplaints avg ~42k-82k mi, $3,200-$3,600 replacement); cooler line leaks (~$550); CVT overheating/limp mode; axle/CV wear; AC and check-engine sensors.
risk_reason: 199k miles with a CVT that has a poor failure record; any CVT service need or failure exceeds $1,000, and original-fluid cars are especially vulnerable. Engine itself is sturdy.
inspect_today: Check CVT fluid color/smell if possible; cold-start and drive for shudder, whine, rubber-band surging, delayed engagement; scan for CVT/overheat codes and recorded CVT fluid change; look for leaking cooler lines; check oil level and blow-by; listen for wheel bearings; check CV boots and AC output.

verdict: 5.7 Hemi is durable overall but MDS lifter/camshaft failure is a known high-mileage issue; 2015 (DS) and 2020 (DT, eTorque mild hybrid) are different generations with different risks. Trucks costly to repair, and parts/labor are pricey.
major_issues: MDS lifter collapse and cam lobe wear (typically 80k-180k mi, $2,500-$5,000+); exhaust manifold bolt breakage ($500-$1,500); 2015 air suspension/electrical (TIPM) faults, 8-speed ZF transmission shift issues; 2019-20 eTorque belt-starter-generator and 48V faults; leaking rear main/oil pan; cracked heater hose; EVAP/o2 sensors; front end ball joints at this mileage.
risk_reason: Both trucks are 190k-211k miles; lifter/cam ticking, manifold leaks, suspension and 4WD components all push likely repairs past $1,000. As-is at this mileage means high exposure.
inspect_today: Cold-start listen for lifter tick/misfire; scan for P0300-series/cylinder deactivation codes; check oil for sludge and history of changes; look for exhaust manifold tick/soot at head; 4WD engagement and transfer case/axle leaks; ZF 8-speed shift quality and fluid; air suspension (if equipped) and sagging; ball joints/tie rods; on 2020 check eTorque warnings and belt; check frame rust and TIPM/electrical glitches.
sources: Owner forums (DodgeForum, RamForum) - web search was rate-limited so figures are from general knowledge

verdict: 2016 Impreza (FB20) is generally solid and cheaper to maintain than the 2.5; CVT (TR580) is decent. 119k miles is mid-life, good candidate if maintained.
major_issues: Lineartronic CVT judder/failure (rare, mostly 100k-150k, $3,500+ replacement); occasional oil consumption (less than FB25); wheel bearings (~100k-150k, $300-$500 each); head gasket concerns are older EJ engines, not FB; front struts and AWD differential fluid neglect; battery drain/ electrical and infotainment glitches; valve cover seepage.
risk_reason: Relatively low mileage for the model and a durable engine; main risk is CVT neglect or wheel bearings and brakes/suspension wear.
inspect_today: Check CVT for judder, shudder or hesitation under light acceleration and ask for CVT fluid service record; check oil level and any oil-consumption signs; wheel-bearing hum; look for valve cover/oil seepage; CV boots; AC; coolant and battery; verify all recalls done (e.g. CVT software updates); tire wear matching on AWD.

verdict: 2016 Legacy (FB25 + CVT) is reasonably reliable, but oil consumption (documented up to 2015+ in some cars) and CVT wear are the concerns; 170k miles is high for a Subaru CVT.
major_issues: FB25 oil consumption (a quart per 1,000-3,500 mi in some cars; short-block replacement in worst cases $3,000+); Lineartronic CVT judder/failure (typically 100k-180k, $3,500-$5,000); wheel bearings; AC condenser/compressor; headlight and electrical faults; power steering/rack leaks; valve cover gaskets and oil leaks; battery drain.
risk_reason: 170k miles on a CVT with unknown fluid history is the main risk; engine oil consumption is another. Routine wear items (bearings, struts) can add up quickly.
inspect_today: Check oil level and color (low level suggests consumption); look for blue smoke at start-up and under acceleration; drive CVT and listen for judder, whine, slip; check for CVT fluid service records; leaks at valve covers/oil pan; wheel-bearing noise; AC performance; control arm bushings and struts; scan for stored codes and check CVT-related TSB/recalls done.

verdict: 2015 Outback (FB25 + CVT) is a decent family wagon but early FB25 oil consumption and CVT wear are known; 144k miles is mid-high, risk depends on maintenance history.
major_issues: FB25 oil consumption (documented on 2011-2015 models, Subaru TSB and class action; short block replacement in worst cases); CVT judder/shudder and failures (100k-170k mi, $3,500-$5,000); wheel bearings; rear differential and CV axle wear; AC compressor; valve cover leaks; head gasket seepage on some cars; battery/electrical gremlins; rust on rear subframe in salt states.
risk_reason: Mid-life mileage, but oil consumption and CVT age are meaningful; wheel bearings, struts, or AC repairs could cross $1,000 quickly.
inspect_today: Check oil level and ask if the owner tops up between changes; look for blue smoke on a cold start and revving; test for CVT judder, hesitation, and whine; check for oil leaks at valve covers/oil pan and coolant leaks; wheel-bearing hum; CV boots; rear differential fluid; AC; confirm CVT fluid changes in records; check for rear underbody rust.

verdict: One of the most dependable large sedans; 2GR-FE V6 with 6-speed auto is proven to 250k+ miles when maintained. Comfortable and family-friendly.
major_issues: Water pump leak (~100k-180k, $500-$900); valve cover gasket and oil leaks; VVT-i oil line (2GR-FE) leak on some; occasional transmission shift flare (rare, usually fluid); dashboard material melting/stickiness (cosmetic) in some; power steering/engine mounts at high mileage; suspension struts and bushings at 190k; AC compressor.
risk_reason: Excellent reliability, but 194k miles means water pump, mounts, struts, or leaks could land near/over $1,000; failures are not likely catastrophic.
inspect_today: Look for coolant seepage from the water pump (pink crust at front of engine), oil leaks at valve covers and timing cover; listen for belt/pulley noise; check transmission shifts and fluid color; struts/bushings and engine mounts; AC; steering play; check history of timing chain noise on cold start; check for service record.

verdict: 2015 Corolla (1ZR-FE + CVT, 11th gen) is among the cheapest and most reliable cars to own; 136k miles is mid-life. Best fit for the budget.
major_issues: Few serious issues; water pump leak at 120k-170k ($400-$700); occasional oil consumption on 1ZR-FE (rare, mostly earlier years); CVT is generally trouble-free but should have fluid service; AC condenser/ compressor; engine mounts; wheel bearings and struts; sticky/cracking dash (cosmetic); starter and alternator at high mileage.
risk_reason: Very durable engine and transmission at 136k miles; likely repairs are small wear items under $1,000.
inspect_today: Check oil level and color; coolant condition and any pink crust near water pump; CVT operation for judder/hesitation; AC; brake and suspension wear; engine/ transmission mounts; any dash warning lights; look for accident repair signs; verify service records and recalls (airbag inflator recalls).

verdict: 2017 Jetta 1.4T (EA211, 6-speed auto) is average at best and costlier to repair than Japanese rivals; 161k miles is high for this turbo engine and VW parts/labor are pricey.
major_issues: Plastic thermostat housing/water pump coolant leaks (~60k-120k, $500-$900); timing belt (not chain) needs replacement around 100k-120k ($700-$1,100) and failure is catastrophic; turbo wastegate actuator and PCV/ valve cover leaks; carbon buildup, misfires and coil failures ($200-$600); 6-speed Aisin auto shift problems; infotainment and climate faults; 7 NHTSA recalls.
risk_reason: 161k miles with a turbo, timing belt, and plastic cooling parts; if the belt and water pump have not been done, the bill exceeds $1,000 and a belt failure would destroy the engine.
inspect_today: Ask for proof of timing belt/water pump replacement (due about 105k-120k); check coolant level and for pink crust at thermostat housing/water pump; scan for misfire, boost or wastegate codes; listen for turbo whine or rattle on start; check oil level and leaks at valve cover/PCV; transmission shift quality; AC and electrical features; look for check-engine or recall-pending lights.
